column3: How to measure
Caliper inside jaws at the stem's narrowest point, 3 orientations; record the smallest.
Caliper outside jaws on the stem.
From the stem's bottom end up to where the bore starts to flare into the cone (sight through the glass).

Stand the funnel upside down, rim flat on the table. Using a ruler or the calipers' depth rod standing on the table, mark a thin line on the cone's outer wall at height a, where the wall first becomes straight below the lip's curve (≈ 4–5 mm). Measure the outside diameter at that line: caliper outside jaws held level, rocked to the largest reading.
Distance from the table (the rim's top face) straight up to mark a. Start: table surface. End: the line where the jaws sat for F4.

Same as F4 at a second line, height b, as high as possible while still on the straight cone: ≈ 3–5 mm before it starts curving into the stem (roughly 25 mm). The farther apart a and b are, the more accurate the angle.
Distance from the table straight up to mark b. Start: table surface. End: the F6 line.
Caliper inside jaws across the rim opening, 3 orientations; average.
Caliper outside jaws across the lip.
Axial height of the lip, from the rim top down to where the lip meets the plain cone wall.

column2: Depth, rim top to orifice exit
column3: Nozzle installed. Straightedge across the rim; caliper depth rod down the axis to the orifice exit. This is z of the rim top.

Nozzle installed, funnel upright. Look through the glass stem from the side at eye level. Find the plug's top edge, then the point above it where the glass bore starts to widen into the cone. Measure the height between them on the outside of the stem with the calipers. Enter 0 if the glass starts widening right at the plug top.
